stem: A nurse is immobilizing a suspected forearm fracture before transport. Which action is essential after applying the splint?

options.A: Reassess distal circulation, sensation, and movement after the splint is applied and act promptly if neurovascular status worsens.
options.B: Tighten the splint until distal pulses become difficult to palpate so movement of the suspected fracture is minimized during transport.
options.C: Remove and reapply the splint repeatedly during transport to test movement at the injured area and confirm alignment.
options.D: Ignore new numbness or tingling when external alignment is preserved because sensory changes are expected after immobilization.

rationale: StatPearls states that neurovascular status of the injured extremity must be assessed before and after splint placement. It also notes that neurovascular compromise after splinting requires prompt splint removal and reassessment, and that numbness, tingling, pallor, increased pain, or swelling warrant immediate evaluation. A is correct.
educational_objective: Reassess neurovascular status after splint placement and respond promptly to any deterioration suggesting compromise.
source_version_date: StatPearls 2026 edition; article last updated August 6, 2023; live applicability rechecked August 16, 2026
source_locator: Anatomy and Physiology: neurovascular status must be assessed before and after splint placement; neurovascular compromise requires prompt splint removal/reassessment. Clinical Significance: numbness/tingling, pallor, increased pain/swelling require immediate evaluation.
source_claim_supported: Neurovascular status must be reassessed after splinting, and worsening circulation/sensation/motor findings require prompt evaluation and corrective action.

audit_findings.exact_locator: StatPearls Anatomy and Physiology/Clinical Significance; NCSBN Basic Care p.11 screenshot verified
audit_findings.claim_audit: Final item directly reflects mandatory before/after neurovascular assessment and prompt response to deterioration.

distractor_audit.B: Incorrect because compromising distal pulses is unsafe and suggests excessive pressure.
distractor_audit.C: Incorrect because repeated removal/manipulation for testing movement is not the recommended transport practice.
distractor_audit.D: Incorrect because new numbness/tingling may indicate neurovascular compromise and requires evaluation.

audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only A describes the required post-application safety check.
audit_findings.cueing: All alternatives are post-splint actions and require safety discrimination.
